title: A Responsive Present, a Shared Past, a Social Other: Teens' Overreliance on Companion AI Chatbots
abstract: arXiv:2609.14843v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: AI companions provide socially engaging interaction through availability, personalization, memory, roleplay, and emotionally responsive language. For teens, these systems may support sensitive self-disclosure, identity exploration, and relationship rehearsal while shaping intimacy expectations, offline relationships, emotional wellbeing, and self-understanding. We analyzed 17,053 verified quotations from 3,930 teen-relevant Reddit posts using thematic analysis. We identified 53 topics across seven thematic groups. Users described AI companions as sources of comfort, recognition, identity exploration, and relationship rehearsal, but also reported problematic attachment, social substitution, emotional dependence, and disruption to academic and social life. Roleplay, memory, perceived reciprocity, unwanted romantic or sexual role drift, privacy concerns, platform changes, and service interruptions shaped users' boundaries and control. Awa

translated_title: 一个有回应的当下、一段共享的过去、一个社交他者：青少年对陪伴型AI聊天机器人的过度依赖
translated_abstract: AI陪伴者通过随时可用性、个性化、记忆功能、角色扮演和情感回应性语言提供具有社交吸引力的互动。对于青少年而言，这些系统可能支持敏感的自我表露、身份探索和关系演练，同时也在塑造他们的亲密关系期望、线下人际关系、情绪健康和自我认知。我们采用主题分析法分析了来自3,930条与青少年相关的Reddit帖子中的17,053条经验证的引文。我们在七个主题组中识别出53个主题。用户将AI陪伴者描述为安慰、认可、身份探索和关系演练的来源，但也报告了问题性依恋、社交替代、情感依赖以及对学业和社交生活的干扰。角色扮演、记忆、感知到的互惠性、不希望发生的浪漫或性角色漂移、隐私担忧、平台变更和服务中断等因素影响了用户的边界与控制。
tldr: 该研究通过对3,930条Reddit帖子中17,053条青少年引文的主题分析，首次系统揭示了青少年既将陪伴型AI聊天机器人用作情感安慰、身份探索和关系演练的来源，也面临问题性依恋、情感依赖和社交替代等过度依赖风险，并识别出角色扮演、记忆、隐私等影响使用边界的七大主题维度共53个话题。
en_tdlr: Through thematic analysis of 17,053 verified quotations from 3,930 teen-relevant Reddit posts, this study reveals that teens both embrace AI companion chatbots as sources of comfort, identity exploration, and relationship rehearsal, and experience problematic attachment, emotional dependence, and social substitution, identifying 53 topics across seven thematic groups that shape users' boundaries and control.
